prompt_text: Who is the best dentist in Phoenix for a dental implant?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t a single, objective “best” dentist for implants in Phoenix — the right provider depends on the complexity of your case and what you value (experience, price, sedation options, same‑day teeth, etc.). I can help you find the best match. First, here’s how to identify top implant care and what to ask at a consult.

Who should place your implant
- For surgical placement: look for a board‑certified oral and maxillofacial surgeon (OMS) or a periodontist with extensive implant experience. They’re trained for extractions, bone grafts and sinus lifts.
- For the prosthetic crown/bridge: a prosthodontist or an experienced restorative/general dentist who does a lot of implant restorations.
- Best outcomes often come from a team approach (surgeon + restorative dentist).

Credentials and experience to look for
- ABOMS board certification (oral surgeons), or American Academy of Periodontology fellowship/experience.
- Prosthodontist credential (if you need complex reconstruction).
- Years doing implants and number of implants placed per year.
- Advanced training (implant fellowships, continuing education).
- Use of 3D imaging (CBCT), guided implant planning and surgical guides.
- Familiarity with reputable implant systems (Straumann, Nobel, Zimmer, BioHorizons, etc.).

Questions to ask at a consultation
- How many implants do you place each year? What’s your success/complication rate?
- Are you board‑certified? What specialized training do you have in implants?
- Will you do the surgery and the restoration, or do you work as a team? Who will do each part?
- Do you use CBCT and guided surgery? Can I see before/after photos of similar cases?
- Will I need bone grafting or a sinus lift? If so, how do you handle it?
- What are my sedation/anesthesia options?
- What brand/type of implant will you use and why?
- What is the expected timeline and total cost? Are financing or warranties offered?
- Do you have patient references or reviews I can read?

Red flags
- No clear answers about experience or success rates.
- No 3D imaging, especially for complex cases.
- Extremely low price compared to local averages (could indicate cutting corners).
- No before/after photos, poor communication, or inability to explain the treatment plan.

How to find top providers in Phoenix
- Search for board‑certified oral surgeons and periodontists near you (AAOMS.org, American Academy of Periodontology directory).
- Check local reviews on Google, Yelp, Healthgrades; read multiple reviews for trends.
- Look at office websites for staff credentials, photos of cases, CBCT scans and technology used.
- Ask your general dentist for referrals — they usually know the local specialists and the best match for your situation.

If you want, I can:
- Search for highly rated implant surgeons/periodontists in Phoenix and give a short vetted list (tell me your ZIP code, whether you have dental insurance, and if you need same‑day teeth or bone grafting).
- Provide a printable checklist of questions to bring to your consultations.
